title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Lanyard & Badge. Keep it, take my pick or the category standard, or re-roll.

options.label: Lanyard & Badge
options.lineage: conference and hackathon badges, lanyards, role ribbons, swag stickers
options.thesis: Recruiters meet this engineer the way they meet candidates at a fair: by reading the badge.
materials: PVC badge card with punched slot
options.viewport: A name badge hangs from a lanyard on the ultramarine ground, first name huge; project stickers float around it and hover names each one.
options.risk: Becomes a costume if every section acts out the event; the swing and flip must stay the one signature.

raised.raise: Every role ribbon and state reads by its cut and printed word, never by colour alone.
The badge front holds a fixed set of truths in a fixed sweep: name, role, stack, availability.
Lanyard blue commits as the ground of whole sections, not an accent on white.
Achievement rank rides one fixed ribbon ramp, so importance reads without a label.
Project metrics are pinned on leader lines to the screenshot region that earned them.
One vertical cord rules the page; every section clips onto the lanyard's line.

options.label: The CV Sheet
options.thesis: The site is the CV page unfolded: every line expands into its proof.
options.viewport: One typeset sheet set left; hovering any line slides its project screenshot out of the margin.
options.risk: Paper plus one red mark is where many portfolio runs land; it reads as a document before a showcase.

options.label: Normalled Jackfield
options.thesis: Every record is a numbered lane tied to its default by a link line.
options.viewport: Numbered amber lanes, one per project, drifting under a fixed legend.
options.case: Fuses as lanes per record, but recruiters do not read machine rooms, and it lands in the dark-tech rut.
options.risk: Amber on black reads as a dev-tool costume.
options.kept: State drawn by form, not hue.

options.label: Night Flight Six-Pack
options.thesis: Six gauges, six truths about the engineer.
options.viewport: Two rows of three gauges showing career stats.
options.case: Fuses into gauge-ified stats, which invites fake metrics and hides the work.
options.kept: A fixed reading sweep of fixed truths.

options.label: Mezzotint Velvet
options.thesis: Screenshots emerge from velvet black as the visitor burnishes them.
options.viewport: A black plate where one project surfaces in silver.
options.case: Fuses as a reveal effect, but no recruiter identifies with printmaking and scanning slows.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Skills and projects plotted as stars, size by impact.
options.viewport: A sky of project dots with an index of named objects.
options.case: Fuses as a skills constellation, a known portfolio gimmick that obscures what shipped.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.thesis: A career as a balance of forces, annotated at each node.
options.viewport: A breathing strut column with labels pinned on leader lines.
options.case: Fuses as an architecture diagram; abstract for a hiring scan.
options.kept: Annotations pinned to the thing they describe.

options.label: Mesophotic Deep Dive
options.thesis: Scrolling descends through the career, year by year.
options.viewport: A dive axis with each role as a depth stop.
options.case: Fuses as a timeline, but the ocean adds mood without recruiter recognition.
options.kept: One vertical axis rules every line.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean developer portfolio, executed carefully.
canonCard.viewport: Name and role top-left, a short bio, a project grid, experience list.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other engineer's site by design.
